attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, as one item in his list of points.

semantics.note: The proposition fairly restates 'hardly the first time AI is helped with mathematics' as a historical observation.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary. It fixes the obvious typo and accepts any documented AI contribution to math research before FunSearch. A single example is enough, which matches the speaker's wording.

evidence.note: DeepMind's blog of 2021-12-01 is a firsthand institutional account of ML helping mathematicians with a representation-theory conjecture and with knot theory. It predates FunSearch by two years. It is a company disclosure, but it meets the contract's source requirements.

reviews.rationale: The claim says FunSearch was not the first time AI helped with mathematics. A dated 2021 account names the method (supervised ML with attribution), the contributions (a new approach to the combinatorial invariance conjecture, and a new knot invariant link) and the date. No counterevidence was found. The support condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post. He puts the scare quotes around 'unsolvable' to rebut press framing.

semantics.note: Faithful. This is an absence-of-evidence claim saying the cap-set problem was not shown to be unsolvable before FunSearch.

contract.note: Reading 'unsolvable' as more than merely unsolved is fair given the scare quotes, and it is the ordinary reading. Tractability is shown by earlier constructive progress. The result depends on that reading, but the reading is not stretched.

evidence.note: Tyrrell's 2022 preprint improves the cap-set lower bound to 2.218^n before FunSearch. This shows the same problem had already seen constructive progress and was not intractable.
The journal editorial confirms FunSearch improved the constant to 2.2202 and notes earlier progress had been slow. That points to difficulty, not impossibility. It does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: Earlier work, including Edel's construction and Tyrrell's 2022 improvement, made progress on the cap-set lower bound. The packet shows no impossibility result. The flagged counterevidence (e2) shows FunSearch's new bound, which does not contradict the claim. The packet admits that an absence claim cannot rule out obscure sources, but on the searched literature the support condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, as one item in his 'In reality' list.

semantics.note: Faithful restatement: the original FunSearch work needed human-written, task-specific code for each problem.

contract.note: Reading 'human mathematicians' as the human researchers, and 'each problem' as each task family, is an ordinary, fair reading of the point. It does not require proof of anyone's credentials.

evidence.note: The original FunSearch paper (dated 2023-12-14) says the input is a coded evaluate function plus an initial program. Figure 2 shows separate code for cap sets and for bin packing. The skeleton is optional, but the evaluator is required.

reviews.rationale: The original paper requires a user-supplied evaluate function and an initial program for each task, and shows separate task code for cap sets and bin packing. That meets the support condition. Nothing shows FunSearch building its own specifications.
